zebralogic.title: Interpret adjacency and ordering clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue describes a spatial relationship, enforce the appropriate positional constraint. For 'directly left/right of' the two houses must be immediate neighbors with the correct direction; for ordering clues like 'somewhere left/right of' only a relative ordering is required.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains phrases such as 'directly left of', 'directly right of', or 'somewhere left/right of'.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'X is directly left of Y' as merely X being somewhere left of Y, allowing other houses in between.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says 'N houses between X and Y', enforce that exactly N houses separate them, i.e., the absolute difference in positions is N + 1. Also handle phrasing like 'exactly N houses away' by enforcing an absolute positional difference of N.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions 'N houses between', 'one house between', 'exactly N houses away', or similar distance phrasing.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting 'exactly two houses away' as meaning there are two houses between X and Y (difference of 3) instead of a positional difference of 2.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: If a clue equates two attribute values, they must belong to the same house. Propagate this binding to all related categories before considering other constraints.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains constructions like 'X is Y', 'the person who ... is also ...', or 'X and Y are the same'.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'Bob has brown hair' as two independent facts, allowing Bob to have a different hair color.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere left/right of Y impose only a strict ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)). No adjacency is required.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrase 'somewhere left of', 'somewhere right of', or similar.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting 'X is somewhere left of Y' as requiring X to be immediately left of Y.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from a particular house or forbids two attributes from co‑occurring, eliminate those possibilities from the search space.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says 'X is not in house N', 'X cannot be Y', or 'X is not the Y'.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring 'Arnold is not in the first house' and allowing Arnold to be placed there.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses. After assigning a value, remove it from the candidate lists of all other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Continuously throughout solving, after any assignment.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same music genre to two different houses, breaking the one‑per‑category rule.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When outputting the final grid, copy each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving spelling and case.
zebralogic.example: Changing 'Bob' to 'bob' or 'Pall Mall' to 'pall mall' in the output.

zebralogic.title: Make forced assignments when only one candidate remains
zebralogic.principle: If after applying all constraints a house (or an attribute) has exactly one possible remaining value, assign it immediately; this often triggers further deductions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During constraint propagation whenever a domain reduces to a single option.
zebralogic.example: Leaving a house's name ambiguous even though only one name is still possible.

zebralogic.title: Disambiguate overlapping attribute values using clue context
zebralogic.principle: When a word could belong to more than one attribute category, use the surrounding words in the clue to determine the correct category before assigning.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During clue parsing, especially for terms that appear in multiple categories (e.g., colors that could be hair or clothing).
zebralogic.example: Mistaking the word 'brown' as a name instead of a hair color because it appears in a clue about hair.

zebralogic.title: Interpret 'next to each other' as adjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that X and Y are next to each other, enforce that they occupy immediately neighboring houses, regardless of order. This is equivalent to immediate adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains the phrase 'next to each other' or 'are next to each other'.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'Bob and the coffee drinker are next to each other' as meaning Bob is the coffee drinker, ignoring the adjacency requirement.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses the phrase 'between' with a simple distance, forgetting that N houses between means there are N houses separating the two, so the positional difference is N + 1.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says 'N houses between X and Y', enforce |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats each attribute independently and does not propagate the binding implied by the clue.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue equates two values, assign them to the same house and remove those values from other houses' domains.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model fails to maintain a global uniqueness constraint for each attribute category.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Maintain a set of remaining possible values for each category and delete a value once it is assigned.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalizes text or forgets to preserve the exact formatting given in the problem.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When producing the final grid, copy each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement.
